prompt: Spotless Sparkle Window Cleaners has recently lost customers because someone wrote a fake, negative review about its service and posted the review online. This is an example of a
explanation: Business tort. Business torts are wrongful acts committed against businesses that cause financial loss. One type of business tort is trade libel, which is publishing an untrue statement against a business that causes damage to the business. The fake, negative review caused Spotless Sparkle Window Cleaners to lose customers, so it is an example of a business tort. It is not a criminal offense because the state cannot press charges against the fake reviewer. There is no indication that this instance is related to competitive strategy. Regulation is not related to this example.

prompt: Jaxon wrote an article that was published by an online magazine. A few months later, Jaxon was surprised to come across his article on a different website. When the magazine found out, it pressed charges because the website was violating __________ protections.
explanation: Copyright. Copyrights protect artistic works, such as written articles, by giving their holders the sole rights to them. The website that published Jaxon's article was violating copyright by distributing his article without permission from the magazine. Patent protections are for inventions. Trademark protections are for logos, phrases, words, or symbols that distinguish brands from competitors. Trade secrets are formulas, processes, or other business information that give companies an advantage over competitors.

prompt: Which of the following is a disadvantage of organizing your business as a sole proprietorship:
explanation: Responsibility for debts. A sole proprietorship is a one-person business in which the owner receives all the profits and takes all the risks. While there are many benefits to a sole proprietorship, one of the disadvantages is that the owner has all liability and responsibility for the finances of the company. Therefore, all debt is the responsibility of the business owner and can be collected from the owner's personal assets. Sole proprietorships are not difficult to set up. However, some types of sole proprietorships require business licenses. Finally, taxation is simpler for sole proprietorships than for other types of businesses because the owner's individual taxes are not separate from the business taxes.

prompt: Laney is ordering supplies from a company overseas. Before she receives her order, government officials will likely
choices: remove the country of origin label from the package.
take a portion of her supplies.
require Laney to obtain a license.
examine the package for prohibited materials.
explanation: Examine the package for prohibited materials. Customs and border protection officials impose controls on any item that enters the country. They are often allowed by law to examine packages, looking for any prohibited materials. Laney's imported supplies will likely be searched by government officials. However, the government officials are not allowed to take a portion of an imported shipment. Laney is not required to obtain a license to import supplies. Finally, it is not likely that government officials will remove the country of origin label from the packaging. The country of origin is required on the packaging.

prompt: Savannah's supervisor asked her to test a new software for bugs while he is on vacation, and he left her written instructions to follow. When following the instructions, Savannah should
choices: repeat all steps to make sure she did them correctly.
skip ahead when she is starting to understand.
break down the steps into smaller parts.
first try the test without the instructions.
explanation: Break down the steps into smaller parts. When following written instructions, it is important to make sure that you do everything required in one step before you move on to the next step. Savannah can be sure she does this by breaking down each step of the instructions into smaller parts. Savannah should not skip ahead when she is starting to understand because each step of the instructions must be completed in sequential order. There is no need for Savannah to repeat all of the steps to make sure she did them correctly; this is not practical and might not even be possible. Finally, trying to perform the software test without the instructions first is not a good idea because Savannah could make a costly mistake without the instructions.

prompt: Your coworker is running his first meeting, and you know he is nervous. How can you encourage him as he is speaking?
choices: Look at your notes so he is not intimidated.
Show interest by nodding and smiling.
Speak up when you disagree with him.
explanation: Show interest by nodding and smiling. One way to encourage a speaker is to show your interest by nodding and smiling. This will show your coworker that you are open to what he is saying. Looking at your notes might make it seem that you are uninterested rather than that you are trying to be unintimidating. While it is appropriate to give feedback, you should not necessarily speak up as you disagree because you will interrupt the speech, which is not encouraging. Finally, paying attention to nonverbal cues is a good idea, but it is not related to encouraging your coworker.

prompt: Which of the following is most likely to be an example of passive listening:
explanation: Casually listening to a podcast. Passive listening occurs when a person listens without giving his/her full attention, such as casually listening to a podcast. Daydreaming during a lecture is an example of distracted listening. Carefully listening to a friend and paraphrasing a speaker's message are both elements of active listening.

prompt: When talking with friends, you might use a(n) __________ communication style, but when talking with your company's CEO, you should use a(n) __________ communication style.
explanation: Informal; formal. Informal communication is communication that is less bound to conventions and is more casual, whereas formal communication is a strategic exchange of information that adheres to conventions. When you are with your friends, you likely use an informal communication style, but when you are talking to your company's CEO, you should use more formal communication. External communication is any contact between an employee and someone outside of the company. Internal communication is communication that occurs inside the workplace. Internal communication would not occur with friends, and external communication would not occur between you and your company's CEO. A passive communication style involves keeping feelings hidden and avoiding conflict. Assertive communication involves sharing opinions and advocating for oneself. Passive and assertive communication styles do not necessarily change based on whether you are talking to your friends or your CEO. Finally, you will likely use verbal and nonverbal communication when communicating with both your CEO and your friends.

prompt: When Rebecca meets with her marketing team, she prepares ahead of time, makes sure participants stay on task during the meeting, and keeps everyone focused on goals. Rebecca is a(n)
explanation: Facilitator. A facilitator is a person who leads a meeting or discussion. His/Her purpose is to keep the meeting running smoothly. In Rebecca's case, being a facilitator involves preparing ahead of time, keeping participants on task, and focusing the group on the goals. A role model is a person whose behavior is imitated by others. There is no indication that Rebecca is a role model. A participant is someone who merely attends and/or works during the meeting or discussion. Rebecca's role is larger than that of a participant. Finally, an autocratic leader is someone who takes full control of the group and makes all of the decisions. There is no indication that Rebecca is an autocratic leader.

prompt: Trent took notes in a meeting, but when he looked over them later, he realized that he was missing some important information. To determine what he failed to write down, Trent should
choices: condense what he has written to be more concise.
tackle the tasks he was assigned at the meeting.
use a consistent, logical note-taking format.
ask a coworker to help him fill in the blanks.
explanation: Ask a coworker to help him fill in the blanks. It can be difficult to capture everything important when taking notes. If Trent realizes that his meeting notes are incomplete, he should ask a coworker who was also in the meeting to help him fill in what he is missing. While it's a good idea to tackle assigned tasks after a meeting, this will not necessarily help Trent deal with the missing information in his notes. Using a consistent, logical note-taking format is an effective strategy, but it will not help Trent after the fact when he is missing important information. Condensing what he has written to be more concise will not help Trent fill in the missing information.

prompt: Gia met Bryce, a potential client, at a networking event. She decided to reach out via email to see if he was interested in her business. However, Bryce found her email confusing and full of mistakes that made her seem careless, so he decided not to reply. This is an example of why it is important to
choices: refrain from using email to network.
allow potential clients to come to you.
explanation: Edit and revise your writing. Revising and editing allow you to make improvements to your writing. Doing so decreases the chance that your message will be misinterpreted or that you will seem careless. Gia did not take the time to revise and edit her email, so it was confusing and contained errors that made Bryce less inclined to work with her. Email can be a great vehicle for networking, as long as it is used properly. Writing long, detailed messages is not necessarily the best way to get a message across. Rather, the message should include only the material that is needed for the reader to understand the key points. Finally, you should not necessarily allow potential clients to come to you; sometimes it is a good idea to reach out to them first.

prompt: How can sending an email expose a business to risk?
choices: Email is too informal for business communication.
The email could easily end up in the wrong hands.
Sending an email wastes a lot of time.
explanation: The email could easily end up in the wrong hands. One problem with using email to discuss business information is that it can easily end up in the wrong hands. Even if you are careful to send emails to the right people, those people might not be as careful, and confidential information can be shared. Email is not necessarily too informal for business communication. Sending an email does not waste a lot of time; emailing is generally quicker than face-to-face communication. Finally, conflict resolution does not necessarily expose businesses to risk.

prompt: When you use an infographic to represent data, your audience
explanation: Will pay more attention. Infographics are visual representations of data. Infographics are much better at capturing and holding an audience's attention than the data themselves. Infographics also simplify complex data and make them easier to understand, rather than causing your audience to become easily confused. Infographics are generally more memorable than a list of complex data, so your audience is more likely to remember your key points if they are represented visually. Finally, infographics do not necessarily cause audiences to mistrust your expertise.

prompt: Niamey is a recruiter who effectively uses her LinkedIn account to attract interest in her company. To build her personal brand and benefit her employer, Niamey should be careful to
choices: use social media outside of work hours.
keep her other social media accounts professional.
be open about her company's flaws when posting.
share personal updates and news with others.
explanation: Keep her other social media accounts professional. If Niamey has built up a personal brand on LinkedIn, she can be of great value to her company by attracting quality employees. However, she should be careful to monitor her other social media accounts because her followers on LinkedIn are likely to seek her out on other platforms. If her other accounts are less than professional, her brand and her company might suffer the consequences. Niamey should use social media within work hours if she is using it to help her attract interest in her company. While Niamey should be honest, social media is likely not the best place to share her company's flaws, especially if she is using it as a professional tool. Finally, sharing personal updates and news with others will not necessarily help Niamey build her personal brand or benefit her employer because it won't help her engage with others on a professional level.

prompt: A problem that is best solved by a group is one that
explanation: Affects many people. While group problem solving can be beneficial, it is not always the best solution for every problem. One way to know if a problem solving group is necessary is to examine how many people are affected by a problem. If it has many stakeholders, it would likely benefit from a diverse group of problem-solvers working together. This approach will make sure all people affected are taken into account. A problem with only one correct answer or a problem that requires limited research might be more easily solved by an individual. Finally, group problem solving can be time consuming, so if a problem needs to be solved quickly, it might be better handled by an individual.

prompt: Your company stresses the importance of building good customer relationships. What should you do if a customer points out an error that you made on his/her order?
choices: Try to determine who is at fault.
Admit the mistake and offer to correct it.
explanation: Admit the mistake and offer to correct it. When employees are honest, customers are more likely to respect the business and develop trust in it. Trying to determine who is responsible for a mistake or explaining why it occurred does not help build a good customer relationship. Simply correcting the mistake doesn't show any concern for the customer's inconvenience or build a good relationship.

prompt: Companies often collect information from the Internet that they can use to identify customer behavior, track sales patterns, and improve customer service. While this practice is helpful for companies, some people are concerned that their information is being used for organizational gain without their knowledge. This is an example of an ethical issue related to
explanation: Web data mining. Web data mining involves collecting and analyzing information on the Internet that can then be used to improve a company's overall marketing strategy. While data mining can be extremely useful for companies, there are numerous ethical issues related to the use of customer information for organizational gain-including whether or not it's okay to gather and analyze someone's information without his/her knowledge. This example is not an ethical issue related to computer firewalls, which are security systems used to protect computers from outside attacks. It is also not an example of ethics in search engine optimization or net neutrality. Search engine optimization (SEO) is a strategy used by companies to make their web content more likely to be shown as a search result on popular websites such as Google. Net neutrality is the principle that Internet service providers should enable the same access to all content regardless of the source, and without favoring certain sites over others.

prompt: A company that wants to present an image of professionalism can help reinforce the image by requiring employees to
explanation: Dress and act professionally. When employees dress and act in a professional manner, it reflects back on the company and reinforces an image of professionalism. Professional behavior includes being friendly and helpful to customers and coworkers. Maintaining accurate timesheets and parking in designated areas are internal concerns that likely would not be noticed by customers.

prompt: How can Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology help a company improve experiences for customers when they call with difficult issues that require the assistance of several departments?
choices: The CRM technology can offer product suggestions.
The CRM technology can collect customer demographics.
The CRM technology can collect real sales data.
The CRM technology can streamline communication.
explanation: The CRM technology can streamline communication. CRM technology can streamline communication between departments, which enables a company to handle problems more efficiently. Customer demographics are usually not instrumental in solving a difficult customer issue. Sales data can help a company determine how to meet a customers' future needs, but are not helpful in solving a difficult issue. Offering product suggestions isn't likely to solve a difficult issue.

prompt: Which of the following is true regarding economic wants:
explanation: They are unlimited. Economic wants are considered unlimited because everyone always has wants. No matter how much you have, you always want more. Economic wants do not stay the same; instead, they change over time. Economic wants do not cost nothing; they can only be obtained by spending money. Finally, not all economic wants are capital goods.

prompt: Price can be thought of as an indicator of
explanation: Value. Price is the amount of money that is paid for a good, service, or resource. It is an indicator of the value of that product because it shows how much people are willing to pay for something and how much satisfaction they believe it will bring them. Supply and demand determine prices, but price is not an indicator of supply or demand. Price is not necessarily an indicator of budget.

prompt: The Valley View Corporation specializes in manufacturing bicycles. Inside the company's factory, you'll find some employees making bike chains while others assemble bicycle wheels or weld metal. This allows the company to manufacture bikes as efficiently as possible. The Valley View Corporation is practicing
explanation: Division of labor. Separating a big job into several smaller tasks is an organizational principle known as division of labor. When employees specialize in certain tasks such as making bike chains or assembling wheels, they are able to perform their jobs more efficiently. The Valley View Corporation is not practicing insider trading in this example, an illegal practice in which undisclosed information is used to make a profit. The corporation may be implementing project management as a broader corporate strategy, but it is difficult to tell from this example. The company is not practicing outsourcing of labor; its employees work in the company's own factory.

prompt: There is a growing need for cultural intelligence when conducting business because of
explanation: Globalization. Because of globalization, there is a growing need for businesses to develop cultural intelligence, an understanding of and sensitivity to the differences in customs, traditions, and values that exist among cultures. Any organization attempting to compete internationally must take the time and effort to cultivate cultural intelligence. Technology can impact a business but does not require cultural intelligence. Economics can impact a business' financial opportunities but does not require cultural intelligence. A business conducting business with or within another country may be affected by the country's politics, but politics are not the reason for cultivating cultural intelligence.

prompt: Innovative managers focus on
explanation: Outcomes. Innovative managers focus on outcomes rather than business functions. Their style is more participative than traditional forms of management. Innovative managers take roles that are more facilitative than controlling.

prompt: In a private enterprise economy, business growth is driven by
explanation: Profit and competition. A private enterprise economic system is one in which individuals and groups own or control the economic resources used to produce goods and services. In a private enterprise system, businesses strive for profits by being better than the competition. These are two factors that encourage business growth by motivating businesses to be innovative and efficient. Governmental regulations do not drive business growth in a private enterprise economy. Risk and price are factors that are involved in a private enterprise economy, but they do not necessarily drive business growth.

prompt: What does a government typically do if its tax revenue is less than its expenditures?
explanation: Borrow money. When the government spends more than it receives in tax revenue, it must borrow money. This money must eventually be repaid with interest. Increasing deductibles would decrease tax revenue, widening the gap between tax revenue and expenditures even further. It is not feasible that the government could freeze spending because it must spend money to keep its many programs in operation. Offering tax breaks would not solve this issue because it would decrease tax revenue even further.

prompt: Valencia invited some friends over to help her make cookies for a bake sale. When it was just Valencia and two friends, they were able to make three dozen cookies an hour. However, when two other friends joined them, they were only able to make two dozen cookies in an hour. This is an example of
choices: the law of supply and demand.
explanation: The law of diminishing returns. The law of diminishing returns is an economic concept that states that if one input increases while others are constant, at some point the increases in output will decline. This means that, if you keep adding workers without increasing supplies and other resources, your production will decrease because those workers will be competing for space and resources. In this case, Valencia had too many people competing for resources while baking cookies, so they were unable to keep up the same level of production. Economic scarcity is the gap between limited resources and unlimited wants for goods and services. The law of supply and demand states that the supply of a good or service will increase when demand is great and decrease when demand is low. Economies of scale refers to the drop in cost-per-unit as a company produces a greater number of goods/services and becomes more efficient. None of these three concepts is related to this example.

prompt: Spending is on the rise, and more people are taking out loans and making large purchases such as houses and vehicles. One reason for this increase in spending could be
explanation: Lowered interest rates. When interest rates are lowered, consumer spending and borrowing will increase because people have more money to spend and are more willing to borrow. Decreases in demand do not increase spending. Higher tax rates decrease consumer spending because people have less disposable income available. Increased inflation can also decrease spending because purchasing power is lower, so people do not have as much available to spend.

prompt: Which of the following examples best demonstrates the impact of culture on trade goals:
choices: A country that values sustainability trades with producers of renewable energy products.
Countries trade for the products that they cannot produce themselves.
A country decides not to trade with another based on political disagreements.
Countries with high uncertainty avoidance generally do not engage in international trade.
explanation: A country that values sustainability trades with producers of renewable energy products. Culture can affect the goals that each country or organization seeks when engaging in international trade. They are likely to trade in ways that support their cultural values. For example, a culture that values sustainability might set a goal to trade with producers of renewable energy products. Countries that trade for the products that they cannot produce themselves are not necessarily an example of the impact of culture on trade goals. Countries do sometimes decide not to trade with others based on political disagreements, but this is not an example of culture's impact on trade goals. Finally, countries with high uncertainty avoidance do not necessarily abstain from international trade.

prompt: Which of the following is a geographic factor that impacts a country's ability to trade:
explanation: Coastal areas and waterways. Geography has an impact on a country's ability to trade. Countries with coastal areas and plentiful waterways are better equipped to trade internationally because they can easily transport goods. Political systems, taxes on imports and exports, and industrialization are all factors that impact world trade, but they are not related to geography.

prompt: When traveling to certain countries for business, you will need to have __________, which is an official document that temporarily authorizes you to be in that country.
explanation: A visa. A visa is an official governmental document that grants an individual temporary authorization to be in another country. Some countries require a visa for business travel. Proof of citizenship is any document that provides official documentation that you are a citizen of a certain country. A permanent resident card is an official document that allows someone to live and work in a country indefinitely. Travel insurance covers losses incurred when traveling.

prompt: Small businesses are important to the economy because they
choices: have a large impact on the stock market.
explanation: Create employment opportunities. Most people are employed by small businesses. Small businesses are responsible for a large amount of job growth and employment in their communities. Small businesses do not always generate large amounts of revenue or impact the stock market, especially when compared to larger corporations. Finally, small businesses do not necessarily indicate future economic trends.

prompt: Taking online quizzes and/or looking at a comprehensive list of values can help you
choices: find gaps between values and behavior.
find ways to critique others' values.
explanation: Determine what your values are. If you are brainstorming to determine what your values are, you can look to an online quiz or comprehensive list of values to guide you or spark ideas. Online quizzes and lists of values cannot necessarily help you find ways to critique others' values, match behaviors with values, or find gaps between values and behavior.

prompt: When Omar's boss compliments him on his recent email marketing campaign, he smiles, says thank you, and tells his boss that he worked really hard and is glad his effort paid off. Omar is demonstrating
explanation: Self-confidence. Self-confidence is a positive belief in your own talents, skills, and objectives. One way to demonstrate self-confidence is to accept compliments graciously. Rather than dismissing his boss's compliment or shrugging it off, Omar accepts the compliment with confidence in himself by thanking his boss and acknowledging his hard work. Arrogance is an inflated sense of self-importance. Omar is not being arrogant in his response to the compliment. Transparency involves maintaining honest and open communications. Omar is not necessarily demonstrating transparency in this situation. Initiative is willingness to act without having to be told to do so. Omar is not necessarily demonstrating initiative in this situation.

prompt: Andre has trouble saying no when people ask him to take on new responsibilities and tasks. Andre is likely to be
explanation: Overcommitted. Being overcommitted means committing to more than what is possible, necessary, or desirable. Andre is likely overcommitted because he struggles to say no to people who ask him to take on new responsibilities and tasks. Therefore, his schedule is likely packed, and he probably struggles to manage all that he has committed to do. There is no indication that Andre is a perfectionist, disorganized, or a leader.

prompt: Although he would benefit from knowing the results of his social media campaign now versus later, Weston is willing to wait until all of the data are collected and analyzed. Weston is being
explanation: Patient. Patience is the ability to endure life's aggravations and difficulties calmly. Weston is being patient because he is waiting for events to unfold in a situation of ambiguity. Weston is not necessarily demonstrating optimism, empathy, and open-mindedness in this particular situation.

prompt: Presley knows that when she hears construction noise while she is trying to work, she becomes stressed and irritable. She decides to bring headphones to work to block out the noise. Presley is
explanation: Developing self-control. Self-control is the ability to manage your feelings, words, and actions. One step in developing self-control is identifying and avoiding triggers that cause you to lose control. Presley knows she could lose control when she is irritated by construction noise. She attempts to avoid the trigger of her stress by wearing headphones, which helps her to maintain self-control. Presley is not showing initiative, behaving unethically, or exhibiting integrity in this situation.

prompt: Which of the following situations most likely requires confidentiality:
choices: You see a coworker's personal social media post.
A coworker asks you to tell him how a meeting went.
A manager wants to recognize an employee's performance.
You overhear a coworker discussing her salary.
explanation: You overhear a coworker discussing her salary. Certain information about other people should be kept confidential to build trust, protect privacy, and abide by the law. In the workplace, individuals' salaries should be treated as confidential. Therefore, if you overhear someone disclosing her salary, you should not share that information with anyone; rather, you should keep it to yourself. You do not have to keep information about a meeting confidential, unless information discussed in the meeting was specifically stated as confidential. Recognizing an employee's performance does not require confidentiality, unless that employee chooses to remain anonymous. Finally, if a coworker has knowingly shared something on social media, s/he cannot expect that information to remain confidential.

prompt: Collin is an introvert, so his supervisor specifically calls on him to ask for his input in meetings. His ideas are always thoughtful and reflective. Collin's supervisor is
choices: challenging him to leave his comfort zone.
explanation: Leveraging his personality type. Successful business leaders understand and acknowledge employees' personality differences. These personality traits can be leveraged to enhance business situations. For example, Collin is an introvert, which indicates that he thinks things through and reflects before speaking. It also indicates that he might be unlikely to speak up in a meeting. By specifically giving Collin an opportunity to share his ideas, Collin's supervisor is leveraging his personality type to generate success. Collin's supervisor is not necessarily challenging him to leave his comfort zone, asking him to demonstrate self-control, or taking his feedback into account.

prompt: Margaret is discussing current events with her classmate Jen when a topic she is unfamiliar with comes up. Margaret doesn't want Jen to think that she is uninformed, so she pretends that she knows what Jen is talking about. What did Jen do to create a barrier to effective communication?
choices: Jen assumed too much about Margaret's knowledge.
Jen was too knowledgeable about current events.
Jen assumed too little about Margaret's knowledge.
Jen started a conversation about current events.
explanation: Jen assumed too much about Margaret's knowledge. When senders assume too much or too little about a receiver's knowledge of a topic, effective communication is difficult. Jen should have asked Margaret if she had heard of the topic before starting a conversation about it. Jen did not assume too little about Margaret's knowledge-she assumed too much. Being knowledgeable about current events is not a barrier to effective communication, and neither is starting a conversation about current events.

prompt: Orlando's coworker asks for feedback on a project. Orlando now has to tell his coworker several things that she could improve on. If Orlando wants to share this information as politely as possible, what should he do?
choices: Follow up with his coworker often.
explanation: Communicate with empathy and tact. It's important to have tact, or the ability to say the right thing in any circumstance. It's also essential to show empathy, or the ability to relate to the feelings, thoughts, and experiences of other people. Being open and honest can sometimes be difficult, but it's still necessary to do it in a polite way. Following up with his coworker is part of communicating consistently. Orlando should not share confidential information. Being responsible for his mistakes is part of being accountable.

prompt: Which of the following is the result of both parties using the collaborative negotiation style during a negotiation:
choices: One party is satisfied, the other is not.
explanation: Both parties are satisfied. When people collaborate, they work together. Collaborative negotiations are more likely to result in outcomes that benefit both parties. Outcomes in which one party is satisfied and the other is not, or in which neither party is satisfied, are unlikely when both parties use the collaborative negotiation style. It is also unlikely that negotiators would be unable to achieve an outcome when using the collaborative style.

prompt: When people lack a clear understanding of how they should speak or act, conflict can occur due to
explanation: Unclear boundaries. Conflicts can surface when people are unsure about what constitutes appropriate behavior and what is off limits. When people lack an understanding of how they should speak or act, conflicts can occur because of unclear boundaries-not because of inconsistent behavior, exclusion from others, or limited resources.

prompt: Marty is motivated to practice his freestyle and breast stroke every day because he wants to break his school's record for fastest time at a swim meet. Marty is most likely motivated by
explanation: Achievement. People are often driven to reach a certain level of achievement either in their careers, in their personal lives, or through their hobbies. Marty wants to break his school's record, so he is motivated to swim every day to achieve this impressive accomplishment. Marty may also be motivated by responsibility, recognition, or advancement, but there is not enough information in this example to determine if he is motivated by any factor other than achievement.

prompt: Kimiko is resisting some new circumstances required by her job. What can she do to increase her adaptability?
explanation: Examine her attitude. Examining how she views the circumstances can help her discover why she is resisting them and develop a more positive attitude. Increasing her level of fear, requesting a different position, or ignoring the situation will not increase her adaptability. Instead, doing any of those things is likely to make her situation worse.

prompt: To be successful in a work environment, an individual leading change must
choices: have a desire to get promoted.
explanation: Be able to encourage teamwork. An individual leading change must be able to convince others to work together to accomplish goals. Anyone can lead change regardless of his/her work experience or desire to be promoted. Change leaders need to help others understand and accept change; a demanding leader that lacks understanding is less likely to be successful in implementing change.

prompt: School grading systems, work wages and bonuses, and sport-related awards are all examples of __________ systems.
explanation: Formal recognition. Formal recognition systems are planned, well-thought-out systems such as school grades, work wages and bonuses, or sports awards. Informal recognition is praise that is offered outside of formal systems, such as a positive comment from a supervisor or a pat on the back from a coach. School grading systems, work wages and bonuses, and sport-related awards are not examples of informal recognition. They are also not examples of instant gratification systems or negative feedback systems.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit of being exposed to conflicting viewpoints:
explanation: Improved communication skills. When you are able to respect and appreciate other peoples' unique viewpoints, you can have constructive dialogue with people of all backgrounds. You will not necessarily be given less responsibility at work or enjoy increased popularity in your social circles by exposing yourself to conflicting viewpoints. Being exposed to conflicting viewpoints does not give you the ability to win arguments easily.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement regarding knowledge gaps and biases:
choices: Not everyone experiences knowledge gaps and biases.
The older you get, the fewer knowledge gaps and biases you will experience.
Knowledge gaps and biases prevent you from making viable decisions.
It's important not to let knowledge gaps and biases influence your decisions and actions negatively.
explanation: It's important not to let knowledge gaps and biases influence your decisions and actions negatively. Everyone experiences knowledge gaps and biases. It doesn't mean that you cannot make viable decisions. The important thing is not to let them influence your decisions and actions in a negative manner. Getting older doesn't mean that you'll have fewer knowledge gaps and biases.

prompt: Which of the following is an external factor influencing organizational culture:
explanation: Laws and regulations. There are numerous external factors that can influence organizational culture, such as fluctuations in the economy, a company's customers, competing organizations, and laws and regulations. The attitudes of employees, the behavior of managers, and company values also influence organizational culture, but they are internal factors-not external factors.

prompt: Which of the following is an ethical principle:
explanation: Integrity. Ethical principles are beliefs that help people make the right decisions all the time. Integrity is an ethical principle that means acting with honesty in all situations. If a person does not follow ethical principles, s/he may face consequences such as lost trust or a poor reputation. Although an ethical person or business is more likely to earn a profit than an unethical one, profitability is not an ethical principle. Security is also not an aspect of ethics.

prompt: Arielle knows that she would be a good entrepreneur because she
choices: likes to see immediate results of her work.
is able to withstand ups and downs.
is easily interested by many different ideas.
depends on others to get work done.
explanation: Is able to withstand ups and downs. One of the most important traits of an entrepreneur is resiliency-the ability to recover from setbacks or obstacles. If Arielle is able to withstand ups and downs, she is resilient, which would make her a good entrepreneur. Seeing immediate results of your work is not associated with entrepreneurship; sometimes it takes years for hard work to pay off when starting a new business. Entrepreneurship also requires a high degree of focus, so if Arielle is easily interested in different ideas, she might not have the focus necessary to be an entrepreneur. Finally, entrepreneurs need to be independent and able to do much of the necessary work alone. If Arielle depends on others to get work done, she might not be well-suited as an entrepreneur.

prompt: Which of the following currencies is considered decentralized:
explanation: Cryptocurrency. Cryptocurrencies are not tied to any country so they are considered to be decentralized. Currencies that are controlled by a country are considered centralized currencies. The euro is controlled by several European countries. The U.S. dollar is the official currency of the United States. The Swiss franc is the official currency of Switzerland.

prompt: Which of the following demonstrates the use of money as a medium of exchange:
choices: Paying cash for a pair of shoes
explanation: Paying cash for a pair of shoes. When money is paid for a product, it is being used as a medium of exchange. When people collect gold coins or save cash in a bank, they are using the money as a store of value because they are keeping it for its monetary value. Pricing a product is an example of using money as a unit of account because the price indicates the value of the product.

prompt: When determining personal net worth, how are personal liabilities handled?
choices: They have to be eliminated first.
They are subtracted from the net worth subtotal.
They are not used in the calculations.
They are subtracted from the total of assets.
explanation: They are subtracted from the total of assets. To determine personal net worth, a person's assets are first totaled, and then personal liabilities are subtracted. Net worth does not appear as a subtotal and cannot be determined before liabilities are subtracted. It is not necessary to eliminate liabilities before calculating personal net worth.

prompt: Rossi is buying a new computer for $363 with his credit card. The credit card has a rate of 24% and uses an adjusted balance method to calculate interest. The credit card company begins charging interest on Rossi's purchase during the first billing period. If Rossi makes a payment of $200 for the first billing period and pays the remaining amount for the second billing period, how much total interest will Rossi pay?
explanation: $10.26. Credit card companies using the adjusted balance method to charge interest only charge it on the principal balance that remains each month. To calculate how much total interest Rossi will pay during the initial two billing periods, first calculate the monthly interest rate by dividing the APR by the number of months in a year (0.24 / 12 = 0.02). Then, multiply the monthly interest rate by the principal amount to determine the amount of interest charged for the first month (0.02 X $363 = $7.26). For the following month, you first need to determine the new principal amount. Subtract the interest amount charged during the initial month from last month's repayment to determine the payment amount applied to the principal ($200 - $7.26 = $192.74). Next, subtract the payment amount applied to the principal amount at the end of the first month from the original balance to determine the new principal amount to be charged interest for the second month ($363 - $192.74 = $170.26). Calculate the interest charged for the second month (0.02 X $170.26 = $3.41). Add together the interest paid each month to determine the total interest Rossi will pay during the first two billing periods ($7.26 + $3.41 + = $10.67).

prompt: Which of the following is the most important consideration in selecting a banking institution:
choices: The bank's capacity to be financially profitable
The bank's ability to help plan your future financial needs
The bank's broad range of services
The bank's ability to meet your current financial needs
explanation: The bank's ability to meet your current financial needs. The most important consideration in selecting a banking institution is whether the bank offers you the services you currently need. While it would be helpful if the bank could help with your future financial needs, it's more urgent to utilize a bank that meets your current needs. An individual may, or may not, need a large number of services. A bank's profitability is not usually a large concern for consumers because government organizations typically insure consumers' bank deposits.

prompt: Xavier has a large sum of money that he would like to earn interest on while waiting for a more profitable investment opportunity to become available in the near future. What type of investment vehicle should he place his money into temporarily?
explanation: Money market account. A money market account typically earns more interest than a savings account and can be withdrawn at any time without penalty. Mutual funds and stocks are typically not good investment tools for the short term because they can sometimes lose a great deal of value in a short time.

prompt: What type of auto insurance coverage will pay for damages to your vehicle if you crash your car into a highway guardrail?
explanation: Collision. The collision coverage portion of auto insurance pays to repair damage to your car if your car crashes into an object such as a highway guardrail, hits another vehicle, or flips over. Uninsured motorist insurance specifically covers injuries to you and damage to your auto caused by uninsured motorists. Liability insurance only pays for damage and injuries you cause others in accidents. Gap insurance is an insurance product that covers the difference between the amount owed on a loan or lease and the amount an auto insurer is willing to pay for a heavily damaged car.

prompt: Which of the following statements is true regarding confidentiality in accounting:
choices: Confidentiality can sometimes be breached for the sake of ethics.
Confidentiality is an ethical principle but never a legal requirement.
Accountants should never breach confidentiality for any reason.
Confidentiality means maintaining honest and open communication.
explanation: Confidentiality can sometimes be breached for the sake of ethics. An accountant must use his/her judgment in difficult situations to know when to breach confidentiality for the sake of ethics. For example, if a client is doing something illegal or unethical, an accountant might feel the need to report it. Confidentiality is a legal requirement in many cases. Maintaining honest and open communication is the principle of transparency, not confidentiality.

prompt: What is the ultimate reason why an accountant must understand current tax laws?
choices: To achieve maximum tax savings for the business
To fulfill all tax obligations for the business
To properly file tax returns for the business
To collect an appropriate amount of sales tax
explanation: To fulfill all tax obligations for the business. There are many laws concerning taxation that affect business, including laws pertaining to collecting sales tax, filing returns, and managing taxes for employees as well as taxes on property and capital. An accountant needs to understand current tax laws to help a business avoid paying unnecessary taxes as well as to ensure the business is complying with all the tax laws that affect it.

prompt: Which of the following businesses would have the most difficulty predicting future cash flow:
explanation: A new donut shop. Since a new business cannot rely on past financial information, it has more difficulty predicting future cash flow. A summer boating resort, a popular tourist hotel, and a 10-year-old pizza place would all have past financial records they could use to predict cash flow.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a finance professional demonstrating transparency:
choices: Evan regularly attends professional development seminars.
Jess makes sure to complete all of her work on time.
Darren speaks up when he sees errors in a financial model.
explanation: Darren speaks up when he sees errors in a financial model. Transparency includes maintaining open and truthful communications. Darren is demonstrating transparency because he is being honest and open about errors in financial data, rather than hiding it or ignoring it. Completing work on time, attending professional development seminars, and keeping financial information private are not specifically related to transparency.

prompt: Why is it difficult for a start-up or new company to establish a budget?
choices: It doesn't have previous data for actual income and expenses.
It has no way to predict how much business it will conduct.
It doesn't have access to accounting methods and tools.
It has no working capital to base its estimates on.
explanation: It doesn't have previous data for actual income and expenses. A start-up lacks previous business experience and data to base its budget decisions on. Companies that have been in business for years are able to review data from previous years to create realistic budgets. A start-up can gather information from similar businesses to help make predictions. Anyone can gain access to accounting methods and knowledge. Most start-ups have some sort of capital to help finance business activities.

prompt: If Thaddeus plans to apply for a consumer loan, why should he avoid using credit to make large purchases?
choices: He will develop a poor credit history.
He won't have enough money for a down payment.
explanation: His debt-to-credit ratio will increase. One element of credit history that lenders consider is the applicant's debt-to-credit ratio, which is a comparison of a person's debts vs. his/her available credit line. The more debt the applicant has, the less likely a lender is to approve a loan. A poor credit history is typically the result of missing payments or revolving credit. There is no indication that the loan Thaddeus wants to apply for requires a down payment.

prompt: In addition to overseeing policies related to employee relations, compensation, benefits, safety, performance, and staffing, human resources managers are also responsible for handling
choices: managing the schedules of senior managers.
explanation: Ethics violations and other misconduct. Human resources managers are responsible for dealing with ethics violations such as conflicts and disputes, discrimination, and harassment. They are not responsible for handling the company's annual budget report, managing the schedules of senior managers, or the company's public relations efforts. These activities are handled by other professionals in the workplace.

prompt: Roger is determining the target market for his new product. Which marketing function is this?
explanation: Market planning. Market planning includes determining activities, goals, objectives, and procedures necessary to carry out those strategies. Selecting a target market is part of that process. Selecting a target market is not an aspect of product/service management, channel management, or selling.

prompt: Which of the following actions is best for employees to take to help their company achieve its goals:
explanation: Use supplies wisely. Thoughtful employees are careful not to waste supplies. They remember that supplies aren't free-they're paid for by the company. By conserving their use of supplies, employees can help their company save money for more important purposes. Attending career fairs, polishing their résumés, and making friends at work are all positive behaviors, but they would not necessarily help a company achieve its goals.

prompt: Aaron needs to start writing an essay for English class, but he's having trouble collecting his thoughts and ideas. What should he do?
choices: Just start writing-it's better to jump right in than to spend too much time thinking.
Use an information organization tool such as a storyboard or an outline.
Write the conclusion to his essay first, and then go back and try to write the rest.
Ask his instructor to give him an extension on the essay's due date so that he has more time.
explanation: Use an information organization tool such as a storyboard or an outline. Organizational tools such as outlines, drafts, and storyboards can be helpful for collecting your thoughts before beginning the writing process. Drafts and outlines are preliminary versions of the finished product that are often composed of just the "main ideas." A storyboard is a visual tool that allows the writer to plan each "scene" or main idea in sequential order. It's not a good idea to "just start writing" when you don't have a clear vision for what you want to accomplish. It's also unwise to write the conclusion first, since the conclusion relies on the body of the writing. It would be inappropriate to ask for an extension on the essay's due date unless there was an extenuating circumstance.

prompt: When analyzing information found online, it is especially important to
choices: use sources associated with political parties or action groups.
assume that the source of your information is credible.
skim the information briefly rather than reading it carefully.
evaluate the reliability and relevance of the information.
explanation: Evaluate the reliability and relevance of the information. There are plenty of online sources that contain credible information-but there are also many websites that you shouldn't trust when searching for unbiased fact. For example, websites such as Wikipedia can be edited by anyone-even people who don't have expert knowledge on the topic being discussed. Similarly, political parties or action groups may run websites that seem to provide unbiased truth, but in reality, their information is severely biased. When analyzing information found online, therefore, it's important not to assume that the source of your information is credible. Rather, you should carefully select the sources that you use. Regardless of the source, it's not a good idea to skim information briefly when attempting to analyze it. Instead, you should read it carefully.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a legal issue associated with information management:
explanation: Customer privacy. Most governments have regulations regarding the privacy rights of customers. For example, a law may state that companies may not give out the personal information of customers unless they receive permission. This is an example of a legal issue associated with information management. Company reputation, quality assurance, and employee training are not necessarily legal issues related to information management.

prompt: Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook are both examples of
choices: virtual reality applications for smart TVs.
explanation: Personal information management systems. Personal information management systems are designed to help you keep track of important dates, meetings, deadlines, and other critical information. Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook are two examples of personal information management systems-not virtual reality applications, mobile geolocation tracking systems, or smartphone operating systems. Virtual reality applications are designed to make users feel like they are experiencing an "alternate world," whereas mobile geolocation tracking systems are intended to pinpoint a user's location. A smartphone operating system is the overarching system that controls a cell phone-such as Android.

prompt: When writing collaboratively, it's especially important to
choices: allow plenty of time for revision.
assign a single person to write.
start writing without a set plan.
explanation: Allow plenty of time for revision. When writing collaboratively, it's important to take extra time for revision so that the writing is cohesive, and so that a common voice can emerge. Writing collaboratively does not mean assigning a single person to write, it means writing as a group. This can be done by splitting up the writing among all team members, or sitting down as a group to determine the text together. It's not a good idea to start writing without a set plan, since writing collaboratively requires that each team member be on the same page. You do not need to lower your expectations when writing collaboratively.

prompt: Which of the following technologies is used to store, retrieve, and update data in a computer system:
explanation: Database management system. A database management system is essentially a software application that handles the storage, retrieval, and updating of data in a computer system. Database management systems help users easily access and organize important data. A peripheral device is a computer device, such as an external speaker, that is not part of the essential computer. The small computer system interface is a set of standards developed by the American National Standards Institute for attaching printers, disk drives, scanners, and other peripheral devices to computers. A CD-ROM drive is a device that can read information from a CD-ROM.

prompt: Which of the following is a primary purpose of data mining:
explanation: To identify patterns. Data mining is the process of analyzing large amounts of information to find patterns, identify outliers, and predict outcomes. Companies use data mining to improve their marketing strategies, cut costs, improve customer service, and more. Data mining is not typically used to locate someone, to surveil competitors, or to attract customers.

prompt: When an angry customer calls and describes an unpleasant situation created by your company, what should you do next?
choices: Apologize to him/her and explain that it will never happen again.
Explain what caused the situation to occur.
Transfer the call to your supervisor.
Repeat his/her concerns to ensure you understand the problem.
explanation: Repeat his/her concerns to ensure you understand the problem. You cannot solve a customer's problem unless you understand what it is. Repeating his/her concerns shows understanding and gives him/her a chance to offer more information if needed. Explaining what caused the situation does nothing to show concern for the customer and is likely to make him/her even more angry. You should not transfer the call to your supervisor unless you have determined the problem and/or need his/her assistance to solve the problem. It's important to apologize and show empathy after you have determined what the problem is. However, explaining "it will never happen again" might sound like an empty promise to the customer.

prompt: It is especially important to keep track of customer sales records because
choices: they can be used to determine what products customers like most.
companies that don't maintain sales records will go out of business.
sales records indicate the total financial health of the organization.
customers sometimes request their sales records from companies.
explanation: They can be used to determine what products customers like most. A company's sales records can be valuable marketing tools. Companies can analyze sales records to determine which products/services are most popular, and which need to be marketed more heavily. It is not necessarily true that companies that don't maintain sales records will go out of business; however, companies that don't maintain sales records are likely to face problems later on-such as when it's time for them to pay taxes. A company's sales records are just one indicator of overall financial health-not the sole indicator. Customers generally do not request their sales records from companies.

prompt: Over the past several years, live streaming video has experienced a surge in popularity. As a result, many businesses now use live video to connect with their customers on social media and other online platforms. This is an example of a(n)
explanation: Business trend. A business trend is a general change in the way that most companies are operating. An example of a large-scale business trend is social media marketing, including live video streaming. Companies now use live streaming to connect with their target audiences on various online platforms. Artificial market, target analysis, and customer profile are not terms used to describe changes in how businesses operate.

prompt: Dylan has been tasked with researching his company's employee satisfaction levels over the last 10 years. After determining that satisfaction levels have decreased, Dylan decides to write a recommendation report for his company. Which of the following should be included in his follow-up report:
choices: A report on competitors' employee satisfaction levels for comparison
Specific, measurable actions that he recommends for improving satisfaction levels
General, overarching goals for employee satisfaction over the next 30 years
A summary of Dylan's experience working with a previous company
explanation: Specific, measurable actions that he recommends for improving satisfaction levels. A recommendation report should include recommendations that are clear and specific, and that have outcomes that can be easily measured over time-not general, overarching goals. For example, Dylan may suggest that the company schedule a monthly social event for employees, where workers have the opportunity to mingle with their peers in an informal setting. As part of his recommendation, he may explain that employees should be polled to see what type of social event they would most enjoy-and polled again for satisfaction levels after several months of events have gone by. A report on competitors' employee satisfaction levels or a summary of Dylan's experience working with a previous company would not be necessary to include.

prompt: When Cheri arrived to her new job at a deli, her manager immediately instructed her to operate the meat slicer. Cheri, who had never used a meat slicer before, severely cut her finger on it. Who is ultimately responsible for Cheri's injury?
explanation: Cheri's employer. Employers are required to have policies in place to train employees in the proper use of equipment and protective devices to avoid injury. An employer is held accountable for the safety of its employees and for the actions of its managers. Employees should use safe techniques and safety equipment as instructed, but companies need to ensure that safe methods are used and followed. Governments provide laws and safety guidelines that companies must follow to protect workers from unsafe working conditions.

prompt: You work at a large company that has a security guard who is responsible for verifying the identity of anyone entering or exiting the building. To simplify the process, especially during busy morning hours, employees wearing their company-issued ID badges are permitted to pass the security guard without stopping. If you arrive one morning and realize you left your ID badge at home, what should you do?
choices: Wave at the guard and head to your desk.
Wait until a coworker arrives and walk with him/her.
Call human resources for a replacement ID.
Ask the security guard to verify your identity.
explanation: Ask the security guard to verify your identity. A security guard monitoring the entrance of a building typically has access to employee records to verify an employee's identity. Asking the guard to verify your identity helps him/her maintain the security standards and protocol. Walking with a coworker or waving at the security guard would not validate your identity or verify your actual presence in the building. It is usually not necessary to request a replacement ID badge unless it is lost.

prompt: How can a company protect its company name from being imitated by others?
choices: Place it in the public domain
explanation: Obtain trademark protection. Trademarks protect the unique names of organizations by preventing others from using them. Items placed in the public domain are available for legal use by anyone. Patents are used to protect original inventions. Copyrights are used to protect literary and artistic creations.

prompt: When throwing a baby shower for her sister, Amy went online to look for information about supplies and the average cost of baby showers. Amy is estimating resources using
explanation: Research. Using research can help you make accurate estimates of your resources. Amy is using research to help estimate the resources she needs to throw a successful baby shower. Amy is not using the past, three-point estimation, or group decision-making.

prompt: Rex is the purchasing agent for a publishing company. His best friend Mia is a sales agent for the Root Paper Company. When Rex needs to purchase paper supplies, how can he purchase them in an ethical manner?
choices: Request quotes from several different paper companies
Contact Mia at the Root Paper Company to buy the paper at cost
Use a quote from Mia to negotiate lower prices from other suppliers
Get quotes from other suppliers, and ask Mia if she can beat those prices
explanation: Request quotes from several different paper companies. It is important for Rex to compare prices from several companies to receive the best price for his company and to allow fair competition to occur among suppliers. Allowing fair competition to occur is ethical because it creates a fair marketplace. It is unethical for Rex to use his friendship with Mia to purchase the paper at cost because doing so could cause Mia to lose her job and her company to lose profit. It is unethical to use a low price obtained in a questionable manner to persuade other suppliers to offer discounts.

prompt: The reason many companies try to achieve high-volume mass production rates is to
choices: produce more products at less cost.
explanation: Produce more products at less cost. Companies use mass production to increase the amount of products produced and reduce costs. High-volume mass production often decreases the number of employees needed to produce items. Production rates are more likely to decrease when a company attempts to increase quality. Inventory levels can be affected by mass production, but they are not the motivating factor for high-volume mass production.

prompt: Which of the following production employees is using a quality control procedure to maintain product quality:
choices: Kane, who is wearing protective clothing to protect against injury
Latasha, who is measuring supply inventory levels to ensure materials are available
Jeremiah, who is reviewing a blueprint to ensure correct materials are being used
Sally, who is counting the number of items produced during a production shift
explanation: Jeremiah, who is reviewing a blueprint to ensure correct materials are being used. Making sure correct materials are being used helps maintain product quality. Ensuring materials are available helps production occur, but it does not necessarily maintain product quality. Wearing protective clothing helps an employee conduct his/her job safely, but it doesn't significantly affect product quality. Counting the items produced helps evaluate the production rate, but it doesn't help maintain product quality.

prompt: A sporting goods store providing snowboard and ski waxing services during the winter would consider the cost of the wax used as a(n) __________ expense.
explanation: Variable expense. Since the store only offers these waxing services during the winter, it should consider the cost of wax to be a variable expense It could also be considered a variable expense because the amount used would vary depending on the number of items waxed. One-time expenses are costs that a business will pay just once when implementing a decision or undertaking a project. A fixed expense is one that occurs no matter what, such as rent, insurance, and utilities. Administrative expense refers to an expense that is not tied to a specific function, such as the costs of executives' salaries and services like accounting.

prompt: Your company has a policy against downloading any outside files. A client has sent an important proposal in a format that requires you to download it. What should you do?
choices: Ask the client if s/he can send it another way.
Ask your supervisor to download it for you.
Download anti-virus software before you open it.
explanation: Ask the client if s/he can send it another way. Asking the client to send it in another way eliminates the need to download the file. Policies that forbid you to download outside files are put in place to protect a company's computers against computer viruses and should be followed. If you download the file or ask your supervisor to download it, you expose the company to the risk of computer viruses. Downloading anti-virus software breaks company policy as well and may cause problems with any existing anti-virus software installed on your computer.

prompt: A pet store retailer and a pet toy manufacturer are coordinating their supply chain efforts. The pet store shares information about inventory levels and projected sales for popular pet toys with the manufacturer. How does this information help the pet toy manufacturer better meet the pet store's needs the following month?
choices: The manufacturer can make bigger profits.
The manufacturer can make better production decisions.
The manufacturer can increase its overall production rates.
The manufacturer can reduce material waste.
explanation: The manufacturer can make better production decisions. Having knowledge about a retailer's existing inventory and expected sales can help a manufacturer determine which products to produce and when. Effective supply chain collaboration can lead to bigger profits over time and reduce transportation costs, but those benefits would not be realized in a one-month period. Material waste and overall production rates are affected by in-house manufacturing procedures and are not likely to be impacted by coordinating supply chain efforts with one vendor.

prompt: When an employee leaves a company, what should the company do to prevent him/her from accessing its intellectual property in the future?
choices: Disable the employee's log-ins and email accounts
Take legal action if s/he shares information
Assess the damage done by the employee
explanation: Disable the employee's log-ins and email accounts. It's important to prevent a former employee from accessing company information. One way to do this is to disable his/her log-ins and email accounts. Company privacy policies should be explained when an employee is first hired. While assessing any damage done by the employee may be necessary, it does not prevent him/her from accessing the company's intellectual property. Taking legal action can help prevent further damage, but it does not necessarily prevent the employee from accessing its intellectual property.

prompt: Ben is struggling to maintain a good work-life balance. He recently began a new job, and the work is more demanding than he anticipated. He hasn't had much time to spend with his family, and his friends feel forgotten. What can Ben do to better balance his personal and professional responsibilities?
explanation: Set priorities. Prioritizing involves choosing to engage in the activities that are truly important or essential to your well-being. For Ben, this may mean choosing to work on his most important tasks at work every day, and then stopping at a certain time so that he can engage in important personal activities. Prioritizing can help individuals focus their efforts on what is truly important, rather than on everything all at once. Multitasking would likely cause Ben to feel even more overwhelmed than when he started. Quitting his job would be unwise, since he probably relies on the income to support himself and his family. Eating lunch at his desk would not necessarily help Ben better balance his personal and professional responsibilities.

prompt: What is the relationship between meetings and time management?
choices: Efficient meetings cover a wide range of unrelated topics.
Meetings are always an obstacle to time management.
If meetings aren't planned wisely, they can be huge time-wasters.
Meetings run smoothly on their own and don't need to be managed.
explanation: If meetings aren't planned wisely, they can be huge time-wasters. Meetings that are not run smoothly and efficiently can waste a ton of time, especially if they do not start promptly and are not focused on the topics at hand. However, meetings are not always an obstacle to time management; in fact, they can be productive if they are managed well. Efficient meetings generally are focused rather than covering a wide range of unrelated topics. While some meetings might run smoothly on their own, most need planning and management.

prompt: In many countries, employees have the right to join organizations that act on their behalf for good working conditions, benefits, and other job-related perks. In other words, workers have the right to
explanation: Form labor unions. A labor union is a group of workers who join together to improve the terms and conditions under which employees work. In the United States, employees have the right to form labor unions and engage in collective bargaining-the negotiating process in which union leaders and company representatives engage to determine the terms and working conditions that are to be provided to employees. Employees also have the right to expect criticism and recognition at work, but this example does not demonstrate either criticism or recognition. Employees do not have the right to unlimited vacation days.

prompt: Harish enjoys playing basketball even though he's not very good at it. His sister Kajal, however, is a naturally talented athlete. In other words, Harish has a(n) __________ basketball, whereas Kajal has a(n) __________ basketball.
explanation: Interest in; aptitude for. An interest is something that you enjoy doing or participating in, regardless of your natural ability for it. Since Harish enjoys playing basketball, he has an interest in it-even though he doesn't have an aptitude for it. An aptitude is a natural talent or ability for something. Kajal has an aptitude for basketball because she is a talented athlete. Just because you are good at something, however, doesn't mean you have an interest in it-Kajal may or may not be interested in basketball. It is impossible to tell from this example whether or not Harish or Kajal have a passion for basketball.

prompt: Which of the following statements regarding job applications is true:
choices: It's okay to omit a previous job if you left on bad terms.
You do not need to disclose any felonies you have been convicted of.
You should never include personal information that is inaccurate.
Job applications require you to have a cosigner if you are under 18.
explanation: You should never include personal information that is inaccurate. It is important to be completely honest and transparent when filling out job applications. Besides being unethical, lying on a job application can lead to serious consequences. If your employer finds out that you included false information on its job application, you will likely be fired-and have trouble finding jobs in the future. Most employers ask applicants to disclose whether they have been convicted of any felonies in the previous five years. It is not okay to omit any previous felony convictions, nor is it okay to omit a previous job if you left on bad terms. Job applicants that are under 18 usually need to obtain a work permit to apply for jobs. They do not typically need a cosigner on applications.

prompt: Joanna is interested in becoming a veterinarian. To learn more, she decided to apply as a veterinarian's assistant. Unfortunately, she got rejected because of her lack of work experience. What could Joanna do to make her a more attractive candidate next time?
choices: Explain her lifelong love of animals
explanation: Volunteer at an animal shelter. Volunteering is a great way for students and other early-career professionals to gain valuable work experience. If Joanna wants to become a more attractive candidate for jobs that deal with animals, she should begin by gaining some experience with animals through volunteering at an animal shelter, zoo, or doggie daycare, for example. She should not make up fake work experiences to include in her next application-doing so would be highly unethical. Offering to work late-night shifts and explaining her lifelong love of animals may help Joanna explain her commitment to the job, but would not necessarily make up for her lack of work experience.

prompt: Which of the following is a benefit for employees who pursue ongoing education:
choices: A greater chance for a raise
explanation: A greater chance for a raise. Continuing education is a great way for workers to improve their current skills, develop new skills, and increase their overall marketability as an employee. Employees that pursue continuing education are marketable to employers because employers want workers who are always willing to improve-and engaging in extra training demonstrates that willingness. Because of this, employees that constantly improve their skills have a greater chance of receiving a promotion or a raise. A highly skilled workforce and greater employee retention are both benefits that companies enjoy when their employees pursue continued education-not benefits that the employees themselves enjoy.

prompt: Fostering a positive work environment, reinforcing company values, keeping employees and customers safe, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations are all benefits that companies enjoy when they
explanation: Implement policies and procedures. Company policies and procedures serve many important purposes, including fostering a positive work environment, reinforcing company values, keeping people safe, and ensuring compliance with laws. These are not benefits of refusing to hire teenagers, engaging in public relations efforts, or releasing annual financial reports.

prompt: One of the benefits of involving employees in the development of company goals is that
choices: employees will better understand how they are contributing to their organization's success.
the company will be able to eliminate training because employees understand the company's goals.
the company won't have as much need for teamwork or collaboration among employees.
there will no longer be a need for monthly staff meetings, since everyone is on the same page.
explanation: Employees will better understand how they are contributing to their organization's success. It's important to involve employees in the development of company goals and objectives so that they understand how their work is contributing to the mission of the company. Employees that understand their company's goals are more likely to be engaged in their work because they know that what they are doing is important. Involving employees in the development of company goals does not mean that the company should eliminate training, lessen the emphasis on teamwork, or get rid of staff meetings.

prompt: Top-line, or executive, managers spend a good deal of their time
explanation: Conducting strategic planning. Top-line, or executive, managers spend a good deal of their time conducting strategic (long-term) planning. Middle managers are generally the ones who engage in tactical (short-term) planning to accommodate top management's goals. Middle and first-line managers are usually the ones who interview and hire employees as well as review performance.
